C30218.title: Row layout: 14 columns in order, blanks in position, bold summary rows
C30218.refs: SV-8622 (SBR spec v24 2026-08-24 S5-R2; Shop Supplies column added in v24; renamed to Labor Delta per SV-9071)
C30218.pre: 1. You are on the report with at least one rep expanded.
C30218.steps:
1. Read the column headers left to right.
2. Read a rep summary row cell by cell.
3. Compare the font weight of a summary row and a detail row.
4. Look for any cell whose content has shifted into a neighbouring column or wrapped; check the desktop Totals row's leading cells.
C30218.exp:
1. With a single location in scope the columns appear left to right: Date, Invoice, Customer, Status, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin, Shop Supplies, Adjustments, Margin, Margin %, Subtotal (14 columns: four leading identifier columns, nine metric columns, and Subtotal). When the Location column is shown — it is shown by default to anyone whose login can reach more than one location — it sits immediately after Status, making 15.
2. On a rep summary row the Date cell holds the chevron control followed by the rep's display name ("First Last"); the date value is intentionally blank.
3. The Invoice, Customer, and Status cells are blank on summary rows; the metric cells carry the rep's totals across all matching invoices.
4. Rep summary rows are bold (700) so they read as parent rows; detail rows use the default weight (400) — row type is distinguished by font weight, not background color.
5. Every row renders exactly the report's column count with blanks in position — a cell with nothing to show is blank, never shifted or wrapped (a drifted row is a defect). The grand Totals indicator is exempt: the desktop Totals row merges the four leading identifier columns; the mobile bar is not a table row.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Sales By Representative report specification version 24 (S5-R2), read on 26 August 2026. The column was renamed from "Inv. Hrs" to "Labor Delta" per SV-9071; only the name changed.
The Shop Supplies column was added to the row layout in specification version 24 (2026-08-24); version 22 stated a 13-column layout without it, and we take the later version as prevailing.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.

C30234.title: Money columns use the standardized labels and definitions
C30234.refs: SV-8622 (SBR spec v24 2026-08-24 S5-R2; S5-R12; §3; Shop Supplies added to labels and Subtotal tie-out in v24; Adjustments per SV-9281)
C30234.pre: 1. A ZZAUTOTEST invoice exists with known billed labor, billed parts, shop supplies, labor cost, parts cost, and tax.
C30234.steps:
1. Read the money column headers.
2. Read that invoice's row values and recalculate each by hand.
C30234.exp:
1. The labels read exactly: Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin, Shop Supplies, Adjustments, Margin, Margin %, Subtotal.
2. Subtotal = Labor Invoiced + Parts Invoiced + Shop Supplies + Adjustments, BEFORE tax.
3. Labor Margin = Labor Invoiced − labor cost; Parts Margin = Parts Invoiced − parts cost.
4. Margin = Labor Margin + Parts Margin + Adjustments. Shop Supplies is part of the Subtotal tie-out but not of the Margin tie-out.
5. The same values appear everywhere the numbers show (screen, and later the exports).

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Sales By Representative report specification version 24 (S5-R2; S5-R12; §3), read on 26 August 2026.
The Adjustments column (the signed net of invoice-level fees and discounts) is included in Subtotal and Margin so every row ties out (SV-9281, added 2026-08-12). Shop Supplies was added to the labels and to the Subtotal tie-out in specification version 24 (2026-08-24); version 22 omitted it from both, and we take the later version as prevailing.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.

C43830.title: Every row ties out once Shop Supplies and Adjustments are included
C43830.refs: SV-9281 (SBR spec v24 2026-08-24 S5-R12 — row ties out: Labor+Parts+ShopSupplies+Adjustments=Subtotal; LaborMargin+PartsMargin+Adjustments=Margin)
C43830.pre:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A representative has an invoice carrying shop supplies and an invoice-level fee or discount.
C43830.steps:
1. Open the Sales By Representative report.
2. On a rep row, add Labor Invoiced, Parts Invoiced, Shop Supplies and Adjustments and compare to Subtotal.
3. Add Labor Margin, Parts Margin and Adjustments and compare to Margin.
4. Repeat on an invoice detail row and the Totals row.
C43830.exp:
1. Labor Invoiced + Parts Invoiced + Shop Supplies + Adjustments equals Subtotal.
2. Labor Margin + Parts Margin + Adjustments equals Margin. Shop Supplies is not part of the Margin tie-out.
3. The ties hold on rep summary rows, invoice detail rows and the grand Totals indicator alike.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582, story SV-9281, and the Sales By Representative report specification version 24 (S5-R12), read on 26 August 2026.
Specification version 22 stated the Subtotal tie-out as Labor Invoiced + Parts Invoiced + Adjustments; version 24 (2026-08-24) added Shop Supplies to that tie-out, and we take the later version as prevailing.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.

C30470.title: Asset cell: Unit # alone in bold; VIN when no unit; Unknown when neither
C30470.refs: SV-8660 (WIP spec v28 2026-08-24 S4-R7; S4-R8; S4-R9; S4-R10 — single-line Asset cell: Unit # alone; VIN fallback when no unit; "Unknown" when neither)
C30470.pre:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The report shows work orders including: one whose asset has a Unit # recorded, one with no Unit # but a VIN recorded, and one with neither a Unit # nor a VIN.
C30470.steps:
1. Read the Asset cell of the row whose asset has a Unit #.
2. Read the Asset cell of the row with no Unit #, then the one with neither a Unit # nor a VIN.
3. Open the column-selection control, turn on the VIN column, and read it.
C30470.exp:
1. The Asset cell shows the Unit # alone, on a single line, in bold. The VIN is not shown in this cell.
2. When the work order has no Unit #, the Asset cell shows the VIN instead, so the cell is never blank.
3. When the work order has neither a Unit # nor a VIN, the Asset cell shows "Unknown".
4. The VIN column (off by default) shows the VIN on its own line as a separate, sortable column. It is the only column that shows the VIN, apart from the Asset cell falling back to it when there is no Unit #. The VIN column shows "Unknown" whenever the VIN is missing.
5. "Unknown" is the same placeholder the shared VIN display already uses on the customer, vehicle and work-order screens; this report does not use a wording of its own.

Note for the tester: the field is labelled VIN. For assets that are not vehicles (for example a generator), this is the unit's serial number.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Work In Progress report specification version 28 (S4-R7; S4-R8; S4-R9; S4-R10), read on 26 August 2026.
Earlier versions of this specification described a two-line Asset cell with the Unit # in bold and the VIN underneath, and Chris Ward confirmed that two-line layout on 5 August 2026 in his answers in this file: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1x8cuYJlFsDHalVZZTh156_ZCq2gcOaGY/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106388879401921597782&rtpof=true&sd=true (read on 11 August 2026). Specification version 28 replaced it with the single-line Unit #-only cell described above (reworded for the single-line Asset cell on 2026-08-20), and we take the later version as prevailing — do not raise the missing VIN line as a defect.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.

C30482.title: An open estimate with no approved work shows $0.00 in every money column
C30482.refs: SV-8660 (WIP spec v28 2026-08-24 Story 4 S4-E1; Story 2 S2-R4; Story 3 S3-R1)
C30482.pre:
1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. All money columns are turned on.
3. A ZZAUTOTEST open estimate exists with no approved line items.
C30482.steps:
1. Open the Work In Progress report and open the Estimates tab.
2. Find the seeded estimate's row and read every money column.
C30482.exp:
1. Every money column — Labor Earned, Labor Remaining, Parts Earned, Parts Remaining, Earned, Remaining, Adjustments and Total — shows "$0.00".
2. The row still appears in the Estimates tab (it is not hidden for having no value).

Note for the tester: this test is about a work order whose status is Estimate, which belongs in the Estimates tab. A work order sitting in another status tab that still carries unapproved lines also shows a second row in the Estimates tab covering only those lines — that is expected, and it is not what this test measures.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Work In Progress report specification version 28 (S4-E1; S2-R4; S3-R1), read on 26 August 2026.
Specification version 22 stated that each qualifying work order appears exactly once; version 28 (2026-08-24) allows a work order carrying unapproved lines to appear a second time in the Estimates tab for only those lines, and we take the later version as prevailing.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.

C30610.title: Thinned history still served by the closest-recorded-day rule
C30610.refs: SV-8678 (IV spec v10 2026-08-24 Story 11 S11-E1; S11-R6; Story 5 S5-R4; S5-R5; S5-N1 — resolved day named inside the "as of" date control)
C30610.pre:
1. Thinned history exists (dates older than 13 months where only the monthly last-capture remains — dev-seeded if needed).
2. The retained capture dates around the requested date are known.
3. To see the information this test asks for you need the browser's own developer tools: press F12 (or Ctrl+Shift+I; on a Mac Cmd+Option+I) and open the "Network" tab, then reload the page. There is nothing to install — it is built into Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Where a check also asks you to confirm what is stored on the server, ask a developer to read it back for you — that part cannot be seen from the browser.
C30610.steps:
1. On the report, set the "as of" date to a pruned day between two retained monthly captures.
2. Read which day the values represent, and read the date control itself.
3. Set the "as of" date to a day whose covering captures have ALL been pruned and where no earlier retained capture remains.
C30610.exp:
1. The as-of resolution serves the thinned history unchanged: the report resolves to the nearest earlier retained capture ("closest recorded day on or before"), even when adjacent retained captures are up to a month apart.
2. The date control itself names the day actually shown — the requested date on its face, and beneath it, inside the same control, the resolved day worded "As of {date}". There is no separate "As of" indicator anywhere else on the page.
3. A requested date whose covering captures have all been pruned resolves to the nearest earlier retained capture, or shows the empty state if none remains.

Note for the tester: this one needs records going back more than a year, and this test system only holds a few days of records so far. If there is nothing old enough to look at, mark this test BLOCKED - do not mark it failed, and do not raise it as a problem.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Inventory Value report specification version 10 (S11-E1; S11-R6; S5-R4; S5-R5; S5-N1), read on 26 August 2026.
An earlier version of this specification put a separate "As of" indicator on the page alongside a date-range control; version 10 moved the resolved-day wording inside the single "as of" date control and states there is no separate indicator anywhere else on the page (Chris, 2026-08-13), and we take the later version as prevailing.
This expectation has not been checked against any build since the specification change described above.
